`budget.py` now takes an optional month: `python3 budget.py 2026-09` counts only September's transactions, and with no argument it prints the same all-transactions totals as before.

I ran it against your data:

| Envelope | No month (unchanged) | 2026-09 | 2026-08 |
|---|---|---|---|
| groceries | 174.60 | 371.55 | 403.05 |
| fuel | 22.85 | 124.75 | 78.10 |
| eating out | 45.75 | 84.25 | 111.50 |
| household | 54.61 | 101.60 | 73.01 |

Two behaviours you didn't specify:
- **Bad month:** something that isn't a month (`sept`, `2026-13`) or more than one argument prints an error to stderr and exits with status 2.
- **Month with no transactions:** a month such as `2026-10` shows every envelope at its full allocation rather than an error.
